questions.prompt: Why are the graphs of y = 2^x and y = (1/2)^x reflections of each other over the y-axis?
questions.prompt_markup: Why are the graphs of y = 2^x and y = (1/2)^x reflections of each other over the y-axis?

choices.text: Because 1/2 is less than 1, so y = (1/2)^x decreases while y = 2^x increases.
(1/2)^x = 2^(-x), so y = (1/2)^x is y = 2^x with x replaced by -x.
(1/2)^x = -2^x, so y = (1/2)^x is y = 2^x with every output made negative.
Because both graphs pass through (0, 1), which lies on the y-axis.

questions.correct_answer: (1/2)^x = 2^(-x), so y = (1/2)^x is y = 2^x with x replaced by -x.
questions.grading_note: Replacing x by -x reflects over the y-axis. The others give incomplete or false reasons.
